newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer did not urge EMU delay - Bundesbank.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer did not urge EMU delay - Bundesbank.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer has not urged either a delay of monetary union or a plan to ensure an orderly delay would be possible, a Bundesbank spokesman said on Sunday, dismissing a magazine report.
Spokesman Manfred Koerber told Reuters: "Mr Tietmeyer has not in any of his talks urged a delay of monetary union or a plan for a delay."
Der Spiegel magazine had cited Tietmeyer as having told bankers that a plan was needed to cover the event of a postponement of the euro launch beyond the planned January 1 1999 deadline.

Der Spiegel said Tietmeyer was concerned that the future single European currency would not be robust enough because of inadequate fiscal discipline among potential participants and had conveyed this message to top politicians, including Finance Minister Theo Waigel.

Tietmeyer has never openly called for a delay to monetary union and earlier this month the Bundesbank chief firmly denied a separate Spiegel report which said he had proposed postponing the euro start.
Tietmeyer then said he was committed to the Maastricht Treaty, which sets down the timetable for currency union.

The Bundesbank and Bonn are currently in discussions on revaluing asset reserves lodged at the central bank after Tietmeyer shot down Waigel's original plan to use profits generated from revaluing gold and currency reserves to ease Germany's path to monetary union.
Present talks are thought to be focusing on currency reserve revaluations rather than revaluing gold reserves.
The Bundesbank has ruled out any profit transfer to Bonn from a revaluation this year, the crucial year for selecting participants for Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
